title: Cheap models: Sonnet vs DeepSeek, side by side

message.text:
**Cost bug, found and fixed.** The GPT-6.1 Sol mastermind showed $0 but cost $3.06, and $2.84 of it had been booked to an idle free-model minion. Both causes are fixed, and a new check (reconcile.mjs) compares our record with OpenRouter's own bill. Today they match: $3.06 = $3.06.

**Paired trial, under way.** Each job runs one Sonnet minion and one DeepSeek V4 Pro minion ($0.21 / $0.42 per 1M tokens) on the same brief.
- Job 1, the line filter: Sonnet is done ($3.19, 10 min, works, no errors). DeepSeek is waiting for free memory.
- Job 2, the cheap ladder on the [Models page](/framework/ai/system/models/): both are queued.

The report comes when both pairs are judged. (This card replaces my earlier one, which was lost in the 22:36 deletion.)

Yes, a cheap model can do small, fenced page tasks. On the Models-page "cheap ladder", DeepSeek V4 Pro matched Sonnet for $0.30 against $1.51, and its version is the one merged. Its one weakness: it can't look at images, and one screenshot read kills its turn, so its brief must forbid images. The line-filter pair isn't finished: the DeepSeek side is still queued because the machine is full (GPT-6.1 Sol's version, $3.06, is the one in main). Send DeepSeek one-page edits with a fence and a smoke test. Keep Sonnet for anything visual or spread across many files. Free models aren't ready. The full report is at /framework/ai/2026-09-30/openrouter-harness/report.md

Both pairs are judged. DeepSeek V4 Pro built a working line filter for about $0.42, against Sonnet's $3.23, but it wrote no readme, doc or tests, and it draws every line twice. So main keeps its GPT-6.1 Sol version. The advice: send DeepSeek small, fenced page edits; a new module still needs Sonnet or a second pass. Full report: /framework/ai/2026-09-30/openrouter-harness/report.md

Correction: DeepSeek's line filter really cost $0.58, not $0.42; that figure comes from OpenRouter's own bill. Servex has restarted, so proxied costs now land in the ledger, and the ledger matches OpenRouter's bill to the cent.
